10-058.r: Indian federalism is 'quasi-federal' (K.C. Wheare): federal, but can turn unitary, generally in an emergency; independent judiciary with judicial review is true but not the reason.

10-059.r: Indian Constitution → quasi-federal (K.C. Wheare), neither purely federal nor unitary; 'federal in nature, unitary in spirit'; Granville Austin → 'Co-operative Federalism'.

10-062.r: 'Quasi-federal' → Prof. K.C. Wheare, in 'Federal Government': India is 'a unitary state with subsidiary federal features'.
10-062.h: Wheare asks 'where' is the full federation? Answer: only quasi.

10-064.r: Co-operative Federalism → Granville Austin; Bargaining Federalism → Morris-Jones; Quasi Federalism → K.C. Wheare; Federalism with Centralising Tendency → Ivor Jennings.
10-064.h: Austin cooperates, Morris bargains, Wheare is quasi, Jennings centralises.

10-065.r: 'Good balance between rigidity and flexibility' → K.C. Wheare: some provisions amended by simple majority, some by special majority.

10-066.r: 'The Constitution has not been set in a tight mould of Federalism' → Dr. B.R. Ambedkar; it has both federal and unitary features.

10-067.r: Herbert Simon → rejected the 'principles of administration' as myths and proverbs.

10-068.r: Law and liberty complement each other: if there are no laws, there is no liberty.

10-069.r: Development Administration concept → Fred W. Riggs: organised efforts by governments to carry out policies and plans for development objectives.

10-070.r: Henri Fayol (father of modern management, 14 universal principles) → stressed similarities between public and private administration.

10-071.r: 'If our civilization fails, it will be mainly because of a breakdown of administration' → B. Donham.

10-072.r: Democracy: people supreme; power with an elected head or elected representatives. Supreme power vested solely in one person, like a king, is not democratic.

10-073.r: Rule of Law (A.V. Dicey): limitation of powers (no arbitrary power), equality before law, liberty and civil rights; 'people's responsibility to government' is not part.

10-074.r: Chief purpose of a Constitution → to define and limit the powers of government.

10-075.r: Constitutional government → places effective restrictions on State authority in the interest of individual liberty, not the reverse.

10-076.r: Constitutional government by definition → limited government; the Constitution limits it in the people's interest.

10-077.r: Constitutional government (constitutionalism) → a government limited by the terms of the Constitution.

10-078.r: Liberty in the positive sense (as in our Constitution) → opportunity to develop oneself fully; not mere absence of restraint or doing whatever one likes.

10-079.r: Equality in society implies absence of special privileges (based on gender, colour, creed or religion).

10-080.r: Only common feature of India and USA here: President's pocket veto (US President must return a Bill within 10 days; Indian President has no time limit).

10-081.r: Barriers to good governance → identified in Report 12 of the Second Administrative Reforms Commission, 'Citizen-Centric Administration: The Heart of Governance'.

10-082.r: 'Unity among diversity' in Indian federalism → Inter-State Council (Art. 263), National Development Council, Finance Commission, Regional Councils, unified judiciary, All India Services.

10-083.r: Indian parliamentary system shifted from centralism to federalism in the 1970s (1971-80), when the Congress lost power in many States.

11-001.r: 'Jana Gana Mana' adopted as National Anthem by the Constituent Assembly on 24 January 1950; full rendition takes fifty-two seconds.

11-002.r: Jana-Gana-Mana: composed in Bengali by Rabindranath Tagore; Hindi version adopted 24 January 1950; first sung 27 December 1911, Calcutta Congress session.

11-003.r: National Anthem → full rendition about 52 seconds; short version (first and last lines) 20 seconds.

11-004.r: State Emblem (from Ashoka pillar, Sarnath, Varanasi) → adopted by Government of India on 26 January 1950.

11-005.r: National Flag adopted by the Constituent Assembly on 22 July 1947, in its fourth session.

11-006.r: Flag design adopted 22 July 1947 (true); wheel has 24 spokes, not 21; width-to-length ratio is 2:3, not 3:4.

11-007.r: National Flag adopted 22 July 1947; Ashoka Chakra has 24 spokes; length to width ratio 3:2.

11-008.r: National Flag's present design adopted by Constituent Assembly on 22 July 1947; rectangular, three colours, length to width 3:2.

11-010.r: Flag Code of India 2002 (in effect 26 January 2002): length to height 3:2 (true); 600 mm × 400 mm is not a standard size (false); wheel has 24 spokes.

11-012.r: National animal → Tiger (Panthera tigris); Tiger Conservation Project started April 1973.

11-013.r: National flower → Lotus (Nelumbo nucifera), emblem of Indian culture.

11-014.r: National bird → Indian Peacock (Pavo cristatus); national tree Banyan; national fruit Mango; motto 'Satyamev Jayate' from Mundaka Upanishad.

11-015.r: Wheel on the National Flag (Ashoka Chakra, 24 spokes) → Dharmachakra, the wheel of law → symbolises Justice.

11-016.r: National Calendar → based on Saka era (first month Chaitra), adopted 22 March 1957; not Vikram era, not from 26 January 1950.

12-001.r: India, a Union of States, is a Sovereign Socialist Secular Democratic Republic with parliamentary government; 28 States and 8 Union Territories; both statements true.

12-002.r: Art. 1 → 'India, that is Bharat, shall be a Union of States'; names used: India and Bharat; States and territories listed in First Schedule.

12-003.r: Art. 1 → India is a 'Union of States'; territory = States, Union Territories and territories acquired; names in First Schedule.

12-004.r: Art. 3 → Parliament forms new States (separating or uniting territory); Art. 2 → Parliament admits or establishes new States.

12-005.r: Power to create new States and alter boundaries, area or names → Parliament (Art. 2: admit or establish; Art. 3: form, alter).
12-005.t: Not the President or a States Reorganisation Commission: only Parliament, by law.

12-009.r: Law forming a new State amends First and Fourth Schedules but is not a constitutional amendment under Art. 368 (Art. 4(2)); simple majority is enough.

12-010.r: Creating a new State → simple majority in Parliament, ordinary legislative process; not an amendment under Art. 368.

12-012.r: India is a 'Union of States' (Art. 1), so A is false; Parliament can alter area, boundary, name of any State without its consent (Art. 3), so R is true.

12-013.r: Altering a State's boundaries does not need the State's consent; President refers the Bill to the State legislature for its views within a set period (Art. 3).

12-014.r: Art. 3: President recommends boundary-change Bill after seeking the State legislature's views within a set period; those views are not binding; A and R true, R not explanation.

12-015.r: Altering a State's name → power of Parliament (Art. 3), not State Legislature; equality before law → citizens and non-citizens; equal opportunity in public employment → citizens only.

12-016.r: Under Art. 3 only Parliament can increase, diminish, alter boundaries or name of a State; a State cannot add territory by itself; 'State' here includes a Union Territory.

12-017.r: Art. 3 → formation of new States and alteration of their areas, boundaries, names; admission of new States is not under Art. 3.

12-018.r: 'Union of States' → States cannot secede (Ambedkar); S.K. Dhar Commission (1948) favoured administrative convenience over language; Nehru-Patel-Pattabhi committee statement also true.

12-019.r: States have no right to secede; Parliament can alter them by simple majority (true). Advocacy of secession is not protected by freedom of expression (false).

12-020.r: States Reorganisation (Fazal Ali Commission) → 14 States and 6 UTs on 1 November 1956; Andhra Pradesh, first linguistic State, 1 October 1953.

12-023.r: In 2002: 28 States, 7 UTs; Telangana became 29th State on 2 June 2014; J&K and Ladakh UTs, then Dadra-Daman merger → now 28 States, 8 UTs.

12-026.r: Goa is a State; Andaman and Nicobar, Daman and Diu, Puducherry are UTs; First Schedule lists States and UTs (28 States, 8 UTs).

12-027.r: Delhi → Union Territory (First Schedule), the National Capital; special status by 69th Amendment Act, 1991.

12-029.r: UT creation years: Lakshadweep 1956; Dadra and Nagar Haveli 1961; Daman and Diu 1962; Chandigarh 1966; DNH and Daman-Diu merged from 26 January 2020.

12-030.r: Art. 240 President's regulations: (a) Andaman and Nicobar, (b) Lakshadweep, (c) Dadra and Nagar Haveli, (d) Daman and Diu, (e) Puducherry; so 240(1)(c) is not Puducherry.

12-031.r: Art. 240 → President makes regulations for Andaman and Nicobar, Lakshadweep, Dadra and Nagar Haveli and Daman and Diu, and Puducherry; Goa is a State.

12-032.r: Dadra and Nagar Haveli were under Portuguese, not French, rule till 1954; Goa full State 1987; Daman and Diu separated from Goa by 56th Amendment.

12-033.r: Sikkim: 35th Amendment, 1974 → terms of association with the Union; 36th Amendment, 1975 → Sikkim became the 22nd State.
12-033.c: Explanation says statehood came by the 36th Amendment, which is not an option; the book prints (c) 35th.

12-034.r: Sikkim → full State (22nd) in First Schedule by 36th Amendment; 35th Amendment set terms and conditions of its association with the Union.

12-035.r: Sikkim: integral part of India in 1975 (36th Amendment); botanist's paradise (Himalayan hotspot); natives Lepchas, Bhutias, Nepalis; all three true.

12-036.r: Sikkim → full-fledged State (22nd) in 1975 by the 36th Amendment Act; its Assembly of 32 members was elected in April 1974.

12-038.r: Mizoram → statehood by 53rd Amendment Act; Mizoram settlement signed 30 June 1986; State formed 20 February 1987.

12-039.r: Arunachal: capital Itanagar named after Ita Fort, two national parks (true); Tripura statement true; Nagaland formed by ordinary State of Nagaland Act 1962, not constitutional amendment (false).

12-040.r: A new State (e.g. Vananchal from Bihar) can be formed only by Parliament under Art. 3; not by State Assembly or Governor's ordinance.

12-041.r: Order: Haryana (1 November 1966) → Goa (30 May 1987) → Jharkhand (15 November 2000) → Telangana (2 June 2014).

12-042.r: Order: Sikkim (16 May 1975) → Arunachal Pradesh (1987) → Chhattisgarh (1 November 2000) → Jharkhand (15 November 2000).

12-043.r: Order of full statehood: Nagaland 1963 → Haryana 1966 → Sikkim 1975 → Arunachal Pradesh 1987; Chhattisgarh 1 November 2000.

12-045.r: Uttarakhand → formed 9 November 2000 as the 27th State; Jharkhand also came into existence in 2000.

12-048.r: Order: Andhra Pradesh 1953 → Haryana 1966 → Himachal Pradesh 1971 → Sikkim 1975.

12-049.r: Order: Nagaland (1 December 1963) → Meghalaya (21 January 1972) → Sikkim (16 May 1975) → Arunachal Pradesh (20 February 1987).
